images.title: Copying an angle
images.purpose: Show an angle at A and its copy at X, built with the same compass settings.
images.composition: Two constructions side by side: the given angle on the left, the copy on the right.
exact_structure: Left: a vertex A with two dark arms; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at A cuts the arms at B and C; a thin dashed amber (#E69F00) chord BC.
Right: a dark ray from X going to the right; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at X, of the same radius, cuts the ray at Z.
Right: a small amber (#E69F00) arc centred at Z, of radius BC, cuts the first arc at Y; a thin dashed amber (#E69F00) chord ZY.
Right: a teal (#0072B2) ray from X through Y.
Both angles carry a small reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arc of the same size.
Labels A, B, C on the left; X, Y, Z on the right.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Same radius at both vertices and the same chord give congruent triangles by SSS.
images.description: Show an angle at A and its copy at X, built with the same compass settings.

image_decisions.why: The matching radius and chord are easiest to follow in two side by side figures.
